Review third-party scripts for unexpected changes and malicious JavaScript.
Alert users to Microsoft 365 outage-themed phishing and inspect reported messages.

learn.explainer: HTTP/3 is a version of the protocol used for web communication. In this report, it is used for stealth command-and-control communication by RATs.
The F-15EX is a fighter described in the report as the USAF’s newest. Its arrival at Kadena is its first permanent deployment outside the United States.
The Strait of Hormuz is the location named in the report of tanker strikes. The report also connects events there with a drone alert in Iraq and rising tensions.

analysis.headline: Access, exposure and pressure across connected systems
paragraphs: The cyber stories show risks at several points of access: HTTP/3 channels used by RATs, third-party JavaScript on popular sites, and outage-themed phishing. Together, they suggest defenders need visibility into both network traffic and the software and messages users encounter. The reports do not establish a connection between these campaigns.

The Kerch Bridge reports describe repeat targeting but leave the extent of new damage unclear. The F-15EX deployment at Kadena is a separate operational development: the first permanent deployment of the fighter outside the United States. Analysts should distinguish confirmed details from uncertainty when assessing infrastructure and force posture.

The Strait of Hormuz report brings together tanker strikes, a drone alert at an Iraq gas field and a US aircraft carrier arrival, with tensions rising. Across the cyber and regional stories, observers may watch for further reporting that clarifies scope and effects. For defenders, the practical focus remains checking exposed services, third-party code and incoming lures.
takeaways: Monitor HTTP/3 traffic and third-party code alongside conventional phishing defenses.
Treat reports of new damage to the Kerch Bridge as uncertain.
Track developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Iraq gas field.
